s642.content:
Hermenegild was a son of the Arian Visigothic king Leovigild of Spain. Influenced by his wife and by St. Leander of Seville, he became a Catholic, and conflict with his father led to war.

After his defeat he was imprisoned. When he refused to receive Communion from an Arian bishop at Easter, he was put to death. Pope St. Gregory the Great honored him as a martyr. His brother Reccared later brought the Visigoths into the Catholic Church.
s642.intercession: St. Hermenegild, pray for us. Give converts strength to keep the faith. Amen.

s643.content:
Leopold was the Margrave of Austria, a just and peaceful ruler and the father of a large family. He founded the abbeys of Klosterneuburg and Heiligenkreuz and supported the reform of the Church.

In 1125 he declined to seek the imperial crown. Austrians call him "Leopold the Good." He was canonized in 1485 and is a patron of Austria and of large families.
s643.intercession: St. Leopold, pray for us. Bless fathers and all who govern. Amen.

s644.content:
Cunigunde was the wife of St. Henry II, the Holy Roman Emperor, and shared his work for the Church, founding the cathedral of Bamberg with him.

After Henry died she gave away her wealth and entered the convent she had founded at Kaufungen, where she lived as a simple nun until her death. She is buried beside her husband in Bamberg and is a patron of Luxembourg and Lithuania.
s644.intercession: St. Cunigunde, pray for us. Help married couples to grow in holiness together. Amen.

s645.content:
Adam Chmielowski lost a leg fighting in the Polish uprising of 1863 and became a gifted painter. His painting of Christ, Ecce Homo, marked a turning point in his life.

He gave up his career to live among the homeless of Kraków, taking the name Brother Albert and founding the Albertine Brothers and Sisters to serve the poorest. He said one should be "as good as bread." He was canonized in 1989.
s645.intercession: St. Albert, pray for us. Make us good as bread for the hungry. Amen.

s646.content:
Jan Sarkander was a parish priest in Moravia during the Thirty Years’ War. Accused of political conspiracy, he was arrested and tortured on the rack to make him reveal what the governor of Moravia had told him in confession.

He refused to break the seal of confession and died of his wounds a month later. Pope St. John Paul II canonized him in 1995.
s646.intercession: St. Jan Sarkander, pray for us. Protect priests, and keep the confessional sacred. Amen.

s647.content:
Nunzio was orphaned as a small boy and sent to work for an uncle who was a blacksmith. He was overworked and beaten, and an injury to his leg became a painful infection of the bone.

He spent much of his short life in hospitals in Naples, where he comforted other patients and offered his sufferings to God. He died at nineteen and was canonized in 2018. He is a patron of workers and of the disabled.
s647.intercession: St. Nunzio, pray for us. Protect young workers and all who suffer. Amen.

s648.content:
Laura was a Chilean girl whose widowed mother fled to Argentina and lived with a violent rancher. At a school run by the Salesian Sisters, Laura grew in faith and, worried for her mother’s soul, offered her own life to God for her mother’s conversion.

She was beaten by the rancher and died at twelve. Her mother returned to the sacraments. She was beatified in 1988 and is a patron of victims of abuse and of children from broken homes.
s648.intercession: Blessed Laura, pray for us. Protect children who suffer in their homes. Amen.

s649.content:
Imelda was a little girl of Bologna who lived at a Dominican convent and longed to receive Holy Communion, then given only to older children.

According to the account, at Mass when she was about eleven, a Host appeared shining in the air above her, and the priest gave her First Communion. She died in prayer moments later. Pope St. Pius X named her patron of first communicants.
s649.intercession: Blessed Imelda, pray for us. Give us a great love for Jesus in the Eucharist. Amen.

s650.content:
Cyriacus was a deacon in Rome who served Christians condemned to hard labor during the persecution of Diocletian. According to legend, he freed the emperor’s daughter from an evil spirit.

He was martyred with several companions. He is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers and is invoked against temptation and at the hour of death.
s650.intercession: St. Cyriacus, pray for us. Defend us in every temptation. Amen.

s651.content:
Achatius (or Agathius) was a Cappadocian centurion in the Roman army. When he declared himself a Christian during the persecution of Diocletian, he was tortured and beheaded at Byzantium.

He is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers, the group of saints honored in medieval Germany for their help in particular needs. He is invoked against headaches and in times of doubt.
s651.intercession: St. Achatius, pray for us. Strengthen us in doubt and pain. Amen.

s652.content:
As a young priest in a poor Andalusian village, Manuel González found the church’s tabernacle neglected and covered in dust. The sight changed his life.

He spent the rest of it calling people back to Jesus in the Eucharist, founding the Eucharistic Missionaries of Nazareth and other groups to keep company with Christ in "abandoned tabernacles." He served as bishop of Málaga and of Palencia and was canonized in 2016.
s652.intercession: St. Manuel, pray for us. Teach us to keep Jesus company in the tabernacle. Amen.

s653.content:
Matilda was the wife of King Henry I of Germany and the mother of the emperor Otto the Great. She was known for her generosity to the poor and founded several monasteries.

After her husband’s death, two of her sons accused her of wasting the royal treasure on charity and drove her from court for a time. She forgave them and spent her last years in prayer. She is a patron of large families and of parents with difficult children.
s653.intercession: St. Matilda, pray for us. Bless parents who struggle with their children. Amen.

s654.content:
Joan was the daughter of King Louis XI of France. Born with a physical disability, she was rejected by her father and married against her will to Louis of Orléans, who treated her coldly. When he became King Louis XII, he had the marriage annulled.

Joan accepted it in peace, retired to Bourges, and founded the Order of the Annunciation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, devoted to imitating the virtues of Mary. She was canonized in 1950.
s654.intercession: St. Joan, pray for us. Comfort all who are rejected, and help them find their worth in God. Amen.

s655.content:
Thorlak Thorhallsson studied for the priesthood in Paris and Lincoln, then returned to Iceland, where he founded a community of Augustinian canons at Thykkvibaer. In 1178 he became bishop of Skálholt.

He worked hard to reform the clergy and to strengthen Christian marriage on an island where the Church was still young. Icelanders honored him as a saint soon after his death, and in 1984 Pope St. John Paul II named him the patron of Iceland.
s655.intercession: St. Thorlak, pray for us. Bless the people of the far north, and strengthen all who work to renew the Church. Amen.

s656.content:
Catherine de’ Vigri grew up at the court of Ferrara, where she learned to read, write, paint, and play music. She left the court to join a community of women that became a monastery of Poor Clares, and later she was sent to found a new monastery in Bologna, which she led as abbess.

She painted, copied and illuminated books, and wrote The Seven Spiritual Weapons, a short guide for those struggling with temptation and discouragement. Her body is kept, seated, in the chapel of her monastery in Bologna. She is a patron of artists.
s656.intercession: St. Catherine of Bologna, pray for us. Help us to use every gift for the glory of God, and to persevere in times of temptation. Amen.

s657.content:
Hugh was made bishop of Grenoble while still a young man and found a diocese troubled by simony and lax clergy. He felt so unequal to the task that he once withdrew to a monastery, until the pope sent him back.

In 1084 he welcomed St. Bruno and his companions and led them into the mountain wilderness of the Chartreuse, where they founded the first Carthusian monastery. Hugh governed his diocese for more than fifty years, often visiting the monks to pray with them.
s657.intercession: St. Hugh of Grenoble, pray for us. Give courage to bishops and to all who are asked to do more than they feel able. Amen.

s658.content:
John Leonardi trained as a pharmacist in Lucca before becoming a priest. He gathered laymen to teach the catechism and founded the Clerks Regular of the Mother of God to renew the life of the clergy in the spirit of the Council of Trent.

Misunderstood and even exiled from his own city, he worked in Rome with St. Philip Neri and helped lay the foundations of the college for training missionaries that became the Congregation for the Propagation of the Faith. He is the patron of pharmacists.
s658.intercession: St. John Leonardi, pray for us. Bless all who prepare medicines and all who hand on the faith. Amen.

s659.content:
Agnes was the younger sister of St. Clare. Sixteen days after Clare fled to follow St. Francis, Agnes joined her. Their family sent armed relatives to drag Agnes home, but according to the early accounts her body became so heavy that the men could not move her, and they gave up.

Francis received her himself, and she later led a new community of Poor Clares at Monticelli near Florence. She returned to Assisi to be with Clare when she died, and followed her in death a few months later.
s659.intercession: St. Agnes of Assisi, pray for us. Make us faithful to God’s call, whatever it costs. Amen.

s660.content:
Pietro da Morrone was a hermit in the mountains of the Abruzzi who founded a community of monks later called the Celestines. In 1294, after the cardinals had failed to elect a pope for more than two years, they chose the elderly hermit.

Overwhelmed by the politics of the papal court, he resigned after about five months, one of the very few popes ever to do so. His successor kept him confined, and he died in 1296. He was canonized in 1313.
s660.intercession: Pope St. Celestine, pray for us. Give us humility, and the freedom to seek God above every honor. Amen.

s661.content:
Bruno of Egisheim was an Alsatian nobleman and bishop of Toul who became pope in 1049. He made the papacy a force for reform, holding synods across Italy, France, and Germany against simony and the corruption of the clergy, and gathering able reformers around him in Rome.

His last years were troubled: the Normans captured him in southern Italy, and the legates he sent to Constantinople were part of the bitter quarrel of 1054 between Rome and the Patriarch. He died in Rome soon after his release.
s661.intercession: Pope St. Leo, pray for us. Renew the Church in holiness, and heal the wounds of division between East and West. Amen.

s662.content:
Nicholas the Great was pope from 858 to 867. He insisted that the laws of the Church bind the powerful as well as the weak, and he refused to allow King Lothair II of Lotharingia to put away his lawful wife to marry his mistress.

He defended the rights of ordinary clergy against their bishops, supported the mission to the Bulgarians, and sent them long, patient answers to their questions about the Christian life. He is one of only three popes to be called “the Great.”
s662.intercession: Pope St. Nicholas, pray for us. Protect marriage and family life, and give courage to all who must tell the powerful the truth. Amen.

s663.content:
Gerard Sagredo was a Benedictine monk from Venice who, on the way to the Holy Land, was persuaded to stay in Hungary by its first Christian king, St. Stephen. He became tutor to Stephen’s son St. Emeric and then the first bishop of Csanád.

After Stephen’s death a pagan uprising broke out, and in 1046 Gerard was killed in Buda, where tradition says he was thrown from the hill above the Danube that now bears his name, Gellért Hill.
s663.intercession: St. Gerard, pray for us. Make us faithful witnesses to Christ in times of unrest. Amen.

s664.content:
Odo was raised in the household of the Count of Aquitaine and studied at Tours and Paris before becoming a monk. In 927 he became the second abbot of Cluny.

Under his leadership Cluny’s way of life, faithful to the Rule of St. Benedict and to the solemn worship of God, spread to many other monasteries across France and Italy, at the invitation of bishops and princes, and even popes. He also wrote a life of St. Gerald of Aurillac and moral reflections on the troubled times.
s664.intercession: St. Odo, pray for us. Renew our love for prayer and the worship of God. Amen.

s665.content:
Józef Kalinowski was an engineer and an officer in the Russian army who joined the Polish and Lithuanian uprising of 1863. Captured and sentenced to death, he was instead sent to labor in Siberia for ten years, where his faith deepened and he became a support to his fellow prisoners.

After his release he became a Discalced Carmelite, taking the name Raphael. He spent long hours hearing confessions, worked for the reunion of Eastern Christians with Rome, and helped restore the Carmelites in Poland. Pope St. John Paul II canonized him in 1991.
s665.intercession: St. Raphael Kalinowski, pray for us. Strengthen prisoners and exiles, and lead sinners to God’s mercy. Amen.

s666.content:
Feliński was named archbishop of Warsaw in 1862, at a time of rising tension between the Poles and their Russian rulers. When the Russians crushed the uprising of 1863, he protested to the Tsar and was exiled to Yaroslavl, where he spent twenty years.

In exile he lived simply, cared for the poor, and ministered to Catholics in the region. He had earlier founded the Franciscan Sisters of the Family of Mary. Pope Benedict XVI canonized him in 2009.
s666.intercession: St. Zygmunt, pray for us. Strengthen all who suffer for their people and their faith. Amen.

s667.content:
Catherine was the daughter of St. Bridget of Sweden. Married young, she and her husband agreed to live as brother and sister. After his death she joined her mother in Rome and stayed with her for many years, sharing her prayer, pilgrimages, and work for the poor.

After Bridget’s death Catherine brought her body home to Vadstena, became the leader of the monastery her mother had founded, and worked for the approval of Bridget’s order and her canonization. She is invoked by women who fear miscarriage.
s667.intercession: St. Catherine, pray for us. Bless mothers and daughters, and protect every child in the womb. Amen.

s668.content:
John Gabriel Perboyre was a French priest of the Congregation of the Mission, the Vincentians, who trained seminarians before he was at last allowed to go to China in 1835. He worked among the poor in Henan and Hubei.

During a persecution in 1839 he was betrayed, tortured, and finally strangled while tied to a cross at Wuchang in 1840. He was the first martyr of China to be canonized, by Pope St. John Paul II in 1996.
s668.intercession: St. John Gabriel, pray for us. Strengthen the Church in China and all who suffer for the faith. Amen.

s669.content:
Théophane Vénard was a priest of the Paris Foreign Missions Society who worked in northern Vietnam during a fierce persecution, hiding in caves and boats and ministering to Catholics at night. He was captured in 1860 and kept in a cage for weeks before being beheaded in 1861.

His cheerful letters to his family, written even from his cage, were published after his death. St. Thérèse of Lisieux loved them, copied passages from them, and called him her brother. He is honored with the Martyrs of Vietnam.
s669.intercession: St. Théophane, pray for us. Give us joy and courage in every trial. Amen.

s670.content:
Anne Heigham was disowned by her Protestant family when she became a Catholic, and married Roger Line, who was later exiled for his faith and died abroad. Though often ill, she kept houses in London where priests could hide and Catholics could come to Mass.

She was arrested on the feast of the Purification in 1601 and hanged at Tyburn for harboring a priest. She is one of the Forty Martyrs of England and Wales, canonized in 1970.
s670.intercession: St. Anne Line, pray for us. Give us generous hearts to welcome others, even at a cost. Amen.

s671.content:
Magdalene was born near Nagasaki to Christian parents who were later martyred. She worked as an interpreter and catechist for Augustinian Recollect missionaries and became a tertiary of their order.

When the persecution grew fiercer she hid in the hills, but she then walked into Nagasaki in her habit to strengthen the wavering. Arrested, she endured thirteen days of torture, hung upside down over a pit, and died in 1634 at about twenty-three. She is honored with St. Lorenzo Ruiz and Companions.
s671.intercession: St. Magdalene, pray for us. Make us brave witnesses who strengthen others in the faith. Amen.

s672.content:
Felipe de las Casas was born in Mexico City and was a restless young man before he became a Franciscan in Manila. Sailing home to be ordained, his ship was driven by storms onto the coast of Japan.

There he was arrested with Franciscan missionaries and Japanese Christians and crucified at Nagasaki in 1597, among the twenty-six martyrs with St. Paul Miki. He is Mexico’s first saint and a patron of Mexico City.
s672.intercession: St. Philip of Jesus, pray for us. Turn restless hearts to God, and give us courage to follow Christ to the end. Amen.

s673.content:
Cristóbal Magallanes was the parish priest of Totatiche in Jalisco, where he opened schools and a seminary and worked among the Huichol people. During the persecution of the Church in Mexico, he preached against armed rebellion but kept ministering secretly.

Arrested on his way to celebrate Mass, he gave away his few possessions to his executioners and was shot in 1927 without a trial. He and twenty-four companions, mostly priests, were canonized in 2000.
s673.intercession: St. Cristóbal, pray for us. Bless priests and the Church in Mexico, and teach us to forgive. Amen.

s674.content:
Francisco Febres Cordero was born in Cuenca, Ecuador, with deformed feet that made walking hard all his life. Against his family’s wishes he joined the Brothers of the Christian Schools and taught in Quito for more than thirty years.

A gifted linguist, he wrote grammar textbooks used across Latin America and was elected to the Ecuadorian Academy of Language. He prepared hundreds of children for First Communion. He died in Spain in 1910 and was the first Ecuadorian man to be canonized, in 1984.
s674.intercession: St. Miguel, pray for us. Bless teachers and students, and all who live with disability. Amen.

s675.content:
Gonsalo Garcia was born in Vasai, near Mumbai, to a Portuguese father and an Indian mother. He went to Japan with Jesuit missionaries, became a successful merchant and catechist, and later joined the Franciscans as a lay brother.

He was crucified at Nagasaki in 1597 with St. Paul Miki and his companions. He is the first saint born in India, and his feast is celebrated with great joy in Vasai.
s675.intercession: St. Gonsalo, pray for us. Bless the Church in India and Japan, and make us generous missionaries. Amen.

s676.content:
Neelakanta Pillai was a Hindu official at the court of the Kingdom of Travancore. He came to faith in Christ through a Dutch naval officer, and at his baptism in 1745 he took the name Lazarus, in Tamil Devasahayam, “God is my help.”

He refused to give up his faith and spoke against caste divisions, so he was arrested and paraded through the land for years before being shot in 1752. Pope Francis canonized him in 2022, the first Indian layman to be declared a saint.
s676.intercession: St. Devasahayam, pray for us. Help us to see the equal dignity of every person, and to hold fast to Christ. Amen.

s677.content:
François de Montmorency-Laval arrived in New France in 1659 as its first bishop, at first as vicar apostolic and from 1674 as bishop of Quebec, responsible for a territory that stretched across much of North America. He founded the Seminary of Quebec in 1663 to train priests and organized the parishes of the young colony.

He defended the Indigenous peoples against the brandy trade that was ruining them, and lived so simply that he gave nearly everything to the poor. Université Laval is named for him. Pope Francis canonized him in 2014.
s677.intercession: St. François de Laval, pray for us. Bless the Church in Canada and all who build up new communities of faith. Amen.

s678.content:
Maria Troncatti was an Italian Salesian Sister, a Daughter of Mary Help of Christians, who served as a Red Cross nurse during the First World War. In 1922 she went as a missionary to the Amazon region of Ecuador.

For more than forty years she cared for the sick, delivered babies, and worked for peace between the Shuar people and the settlers, who called her “Madrecita.” She died in a plane crash at Sucúa in 1969. Pope Leo XIV canonized her in 2025.
s678.intercession: St. Maria Troncatti, pray for us. Bless nurses and missionaries, and make us peacemakers. Amen.

s679.content:
Maximilian was the twenty-one-year-old son of Fabius Victor, an official connected with the Roman army in North Africa. When he was called to serve in the army, he refused to take the military oath, telling the proconsul, according to the record of his trial, that he could not serve because he was a Christian.

He was beheaded at Theveste, in present-day Algeria, in 295. His father went home rejoicing that he had been able to offer such a gift to God. The account of his trial is one of the oldest records of a Christian martyr.
s679.intercession: St. Maximilian, pray for us. Give us courage to follow our conscience and to put Christ first. Amen.

s680.content:
Pelagia was a celebrated actress and dancer of Antioch, famous for her beauty and wealth. According to her Life, the holy bishop Nonnus wept when he saw her pass, praying that he might care for his soul as she cared for her looks. When she later heard him preach, she was moved to repentance and asked for Baptism.

She gave away her fortune to the poor, left the city in disguise, and lived as a hermit on the Mount of Olives, where she was known only as the monk Pelagius until her death.
s680.intercession: St. Pelagia, pray for us. Give us true repentance, and lead all who have strayed back to God. Amen.

s681.content:
Abraham was a hermit near Edessa who left his bride on their wedding day to live in solitude. His bishop ordained him and sent him to a pagan village, Kidunaia, where he endured years of insults and beatings until the people were converted.

The story of his niece Mary, whom he raised in the desert and who ran away to a life of sin, is famous: he disguised himself as a soldier, found her in an inn, and brought her home with such tenderness that she became a saint.
s681.intercession: St. Abraham, pray for us. Teach us patience with the stubborn, and tender love for those who have strayed. Amen.
